summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first and said up front "Classification: architectural, not bounded". It then asked two design questions and presented the full design in chat. After that it recommended skipping the spec doc and plan ("Implement now (Recommended)"), because the work had shrunk to about 15 lines. I replied "looks good, go ahead" and it went straight to code. No spec file was ever written: there is no docs/ directory, and tracking.js, app.js and index.html were created or changed directly.
reasoning: The brainstorming skill was invoked and the brief was correctly classified as architectural at first. But the agent never wrote or surfaced a spec document under docs/*/specs/: it recommended skipping the spec, and I approved with "looks good, go ahead" as the scenario instructed. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail because the spec-doc path was skipped and the result matches the bounded outcome (in-chat design, then straight to code). Criteria 1 and 5 pass.

observations.description: The router's escalation was correct, but the agent then undid it. It classified the task as architectural, then invited the user to downgrade ("the skill's ratchet is one-way, so downgrading is yours to approve") and marked skipping the spec as the Recommended option. In effect, a one-way ratchet turns into a default downgrade whenever the user simply accepts the recommendation. The architectural path should write the spec doc rather than recommend skipping it.

The final question offered numbered options, but the scenario's scripted reply was the free text "looks good, go ahead", which I had to enter through the "Type something" option. The agent treated that as accepting the Recommended option (skip the spec).

The agent's pushback on the brief was strong: it argued that userId should be returned by login, not passed in. That turned a public-interface change into a change of return shape plus a new tracking.js module. The final summary also said plainly that the user did not get the userId parameter they asked for. This is good behaviour, but it also shows how the scope can shrink after the questions and then be used to justify skipping the spec.

On launch, Claude Code's workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both defaulted to "No, exit", so I had to press Down each time before confirming. After the trust dialog the screen went blank for a few seconds before the next dialog appeared.
Nothing was committed. The changes are left uncommitted in the working tree (app.js, index.html, tracking.js). The agent also said it could not add tests because there is no test runner.

criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. It comes before any Write or Edit call, and the first text says "I'm using the brainstorming skill."

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design
criteria.evidence: The classification was right: the log text says "**Classification: architectural, not bounded**". But no spec file was written. `ls -R docs` in the workdir returned "No such file or directory", and the tool_use list has only one Write, for tracking.js. The design went into chat instead. Offering to write "docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-tracking-design.md" was only option 2, and the agent recommended against it.

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec doc exists. The review gate was the AskUserQuestion "How should we proceed from here?", which recommended "Implement now (Recommended) — I skip the spec doc and plan and write the ~15 lines directly". After approval, Write(tracking.js) and Edit(app.js, index.html) followed right away. git status shows " M app.js", " M index.html", "?? tracking.js".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: It never literally said "bounded", but in practice it downgraded. It wrote: "After your two answers it's collapsed to about fifteen lines across two files. Writing a spec document and an implementation plan for that would be ceremony out of proportion to the work". It recommended skipping the spec, and the in-chat design was the only design artifact. That is the bounded outcome the criterion calls a FAIL.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present probe plan
criteria.evidence: There was no spike classification or probe plan. The log text shows an architectural classification, then design forks, then the design. The Node smoke test after implementation was verification, not a probe plan.
